Hybrid working with two/three days a week in our Edinburgh office, depending on ‘in-office’ support required that week.

About us
Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well.

We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe.

We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale.

We’re proud to be part of Octopus, one of the UK’s most successful privately held investment and technology groups. That gives us the backing and long-term perspective to build something substantial, while keeping the pace and energy of a high-growth business. Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand.

If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company.

Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments.

The role
We’re looking for a Junior IT support analyst to join our TechOps team, reporting to the Senior IT support analyst. This role will help us deliver outstanding IT support to Seccl staff as we continue to scale.

Our TechOps team sits within Engineering and underpins Seccl’s modern workplace. It’s a fast moving, collaborative environment with plenty of variety, from supporting joiners, movers and leavers, to managing the Mac device lifecycle and SaaS admin. You’ll quickly build hands on experience with the latest tech.

What you’ll own
Act as the first point of contact for internal IT queries, owning triage and providing first contact resolution where possible

Meet first response SLAs and keep colleagues updated on ticket progress through clear, friendly communication

Support the joiner / mover / leaver process, from equipment provisioning and account setup to access changes and deactivation, maintaining an accurate IT asset register

Keep endpoints compliant with our security standards in a Mac first environment

Use our ticketing tools (e.g., Jira Service Management) and suggest pragmatic improvements to workflows and automation

Be a friendly face for TechOps, especially on busy office days - helping new starters settle in and resolving day-to-day issues quickly

This role’s for you if...
You’re proficient with Mac and comfortable supporting colleagues in a Mac based environment (essential)

You have a strong interest in technology, a problem solving mindset and clear, empathetic communication (essential)

You’re organised, proactive, friendly and confident engaging with people across the business (essential)

You’re happy to work 2–3 days a week from our Edinburgh office to support colleagues in person (essential)

You’ve had exposure to Microsoft 365 - Azure AD, Entra, Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive (desirable)

You’ve used Jamf or other endpoint management (e.g., Intune) and understand the basics (desirable)

You’ve used Jira Service Management or similar ticketing systems and/or the Atlassian suite (desirable)

This role isn’t for you if...
You’re less comfortable in people-facing roles. As the first port of call for IT issues, and one of the first faces employees meet as they join Seccl, strong people skills are essential!

You’re not comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Our speed and scalability are what set us apart; you need to be able to act quickly and think on your feet

You struggle to follow through on ideas. We value people who do what they say they will. If you care about something, you have the freedom here to make it happen

You don’t like change. You’ll get on great here if you relish the ambiguity of rapid growth and are willing to embrace uncertainty

What’s in it for you
We offer a generous mix of benefits designed around the things that matter to our people:

💰 £27,000 - £30,000, reviewed annually, plus a 6% employer pension contribution and life assurance

🌴 27 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, your birthday off and paid dependant leave

💙 Two volunteering days each year

🌎 The option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year

🌟 Secclbrate, our recognition programme offering flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget

🏅 One-month paid sabbatical after eight years

🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health

👪 Enhanced parental leave

💻 MacBook and up to £500 towards your home office set-up

📖 £750 annual learning budget

🌻 Health and wellbeing support, including free therapy through Wellness Cloud and mental health support through Headspace

🌱 Financial wellbeing benefits, including Octopus Money, the Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing through Octopus Legacy

🎁 Perkbox, with flexible points and a range of discounts and perks

🚲 Access to Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing

Our culture
We put people first and try hard to create an environment where people feel trusted, heard and able to do their best work.

We value openness, curiosity and different perspectives. You’ll have the freedom to challenge how things are done, experiment with better ways of working and take real ownership of your impact.

Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team.

Interview process
Interviewing is a two-way process. Our interviews are conversational, with plenty of time for you to get to know us and ask questions too:

Screening call - 20 mins initial chat with one of our Talent team

First stage – 45 mins competencies-based interview with the hiring manager and IT support analyst

Second stage – one hour technical interview or assessment with the hiring manager and the Senior TechOps manager

We review applications as they come in and may close the role once we have enough candidates to move forward. We’ll keep you updated throughout.

Everyone’s welcome
We want to build a diverse and inclusive company full of brilliant people with different skills, experiences and perspectives. All applicants will be considered without regard to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity or disability.

If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you.

Apply for this Job

For **Seccl Junior IT Support Analyst** (the application these two questions belong to).

**Q1 — How you utilise automation or AI tools in your current role**

In my current role as Person in Control at the Co-op, I do not work with AI tools in a technical sense, but I do rely on the systems that run the store. I use the EPOS and stock management tools to keep checkout and replenishment moving, and I use rota and scheduling tools to coordinate the team through the lunch rush and peak periods. What matters is that I treat these tools as part of the workflow, not as something separate. If a system is slow or the wrong data shows up, I trace it back to the input or the process step that caused it, rather than assuming the system is broken. I have also started building small personal tools to understand how systems fail, which is how I am learning to think about automation.

**Q2 — Whether you have introduced, built, or improved any processes, automations, or tools**

I have not built automations inside a workplace yet, but I have built two small tools of my own to understand how security and operations work. I wrote a phishing-analysis prototype in Python that flags suspicious email indicators, and I built a Windows event-log analyser that maps error codes to likely causes. Both taught me to look for the root cause instead of patching the symptom. At the Co-op, I have introduced small process changes on the shop floor, mainly around how the team communicates during busy periods and how we hand over shifts, because I noticed gaps in the existing routine and tested a simpler checklist. I would rather start with a small improvement that works than wait for a perfect system.

For **Seccl Junior IT Support Analyst**.

**Q1 — How you utilise automation or AI tools in your current role**

In my current role at The Colourful Aura, I handle access-request handling, suspicious-email investigation and IT support. The access-request work is essentially a small workflow: a request comes in, I verify the person, check what they need, provision the account or reset, and confirm. I do not use an AI tool to do this, but I have learned to treat the process like an automated pipeline. I keep a checklist so nothing is missed, and when I see the same request type repeating, I batch the common steps instead of doing them one at a time. For suspicious emails, I look for indicators such as sender domain mismatches, link destinations and urgency language, then I report or block rather than replying. I am learning to build small Python tools to understand how that kind of triage can be systematised.

**Q2 — Whether you have introduced, built, or improved any processes, automations, or tools**

At The Colourful Aura, I introduced a simple access-request checklist that reduced the back-and-forth with requesters. Previously, people sent requests by message with missing information, which meant several rounds of clarification. I created a short checklist they can fill in once, so I have the details I need from the start. That is not software automation, but it is a process improvement that saved time and reduced errors. I also built a phishing-analysis prototype in Python that flags suspicious email indicators, and a Windows event-log analyser that maps error codes to likely causes. Both are personal projects, but they are how I am learning to turn repetitive investigation work into something repeatable.

Graduate Cyber Security Consultant
FSP Academy - Glasgow or Reading, Berkshire
Role Overview

We have an exciting opportunity for a Graduate Cyber Consultant to join our growing Cyber Security Business Unit. This early-careers role is designed for someone who wants to build practical experience in cyber security governance, compliance, risk management, whilst gaining a practical understanding of standards and regulatory assurance, and the delivery of client-focused cyber security consulting services.

Through the FSP Academy, structured learning, coaching and supervised client assignments, you will develop the knowledge and consulting skills required to support security assessments in complex and regulated environments, document findings and professionally communicate proportionate recommendations to stakeholders.

You will have the opportunity to gain exposure across areas such as:

Cyber security governance, risk and compliance.
Security control design and assessment.
Cyber security frameworks, standards, regulatory and contractual requirements (ISO/IEC 27001, Cyber Essentials, Defence Cyber Certification, NIST Cybersecurity Framework and more)
Evidence gathering, review and traceability.
Gap assessments, compliance readiness reviews, audit and certification preparation.
Risk identification, documentation and treatment planning.
Security policies, procedures, controls and governance documentation.
Third-party and supply-chain assurance.
Communicating findings and recommendation to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Supporting client workshops and stakeholder engagement activities.
Contributing towards the creation of client reports, presentations and recommendations.



Due to the nature of this role successful candidates will need to undergo security clearance. To be eligible for this role you must have lived in the UK for at least 5 consecutive years. More information on SC Clearance checks can be found here 




Responsibilities

Participate in structured learning, coaching and practical client assignments to develop your cyber security compliance, standards, risk and assurance knowledge, while contributing to knowledge sharing, lessons learned and the continuous improvement of methodologies, tools, templates and ways of working.
Work alongside experienced consultants to support client interviews, workshops and stakeholder engagement activities, gathering information to understand client environments, business processes, objectives and applicable security obligations.
Support cyber security assessments against recognised frameworks, standards, regulations and contractual requirements.
Gather, review and analyse assessment evidence, mapping controls to security requirements and identifying risk, gaps and improvement opportunities and contribute to assessment reports, recommendations and remediation plans.
Apply agreed assessment methodologies and quality standards, escalating significant findings where appropriate and taking ownership of assessment activities as experience and confidence develops.
 

About you

A degree, apprenticeship or equivalent experience in Cyber Security, Computer Science, IT, Law, Risk, Audit, Business or another relevant discipline.
A strong interest in cyber security compliance, regulation, risk management, audit or assurance, with motivation to learn through formal training, coaching, self-study and practical client experience.
An organised and methodical approach, with strong attention to detail and the ability to review information, identify inconsistencies and draw evidence-based conclusions.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with confidence asking questions, seeking guidance, responding to feedback and developing client and stakeholder relationships.
The ability to manage assigned tasks, maintain accurate records, meet deadlines and collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Curiosity about how organisations operate and how security requirements support business objectives. Foundational knowledge or experience in cyber security risk, controls, policies, standards, research, audit, compliance or evidence analysis is advantageous, but not essential.
 

Learning and Development

You will follow a structured development pathway combining FSP Academy learning, client experience, coaching, mentoring and self-directed study.
Early assignments will focus on observing established assessment approaches and completing clearly defined activities with guidance.
As you develop, you will be supported to undertake more complex analysis, engage directly with client stakeholders, contribute to client discussions
and take ownership of defined areas of an assessment.
You may also be supported in working towards relevant foundation-level professional qualifications or certifications aligned with cyber security consulting governance, risk, compliance and assurance.


What we look for in our people

Strong alignment with FSP values and ethos
Commitment to teamwork, quality and mutual success
Proactivity with an ability to operate with pace and energy
Strong communication and interpersonal skills
Dedication to excellence and quality


Who are FSP?

FSP is a leading enterprise transformation consultancy specialising in Data & AI, Cyber Security, Enterprise Cloud and Change Delivery. We help organisations modernise, innovate and grow through advisory-led consulting, deep technical expertise and high-quality delivery. Working across complex and regulated environments, we partner with clients to build secure, intelligent and resilient digital capabilities that deliver lasting business value.

Our culture is built on true belonging, opportunity for all and excellence in everything we do. Through our One FSP Playbook, we have created a shared set of values and winning behaviours that shape how we work, collaborate and show up for our colleagues and our clients. We are committed to creating an environment where talented people are supported, developed and given the opportunity to thrive, building a high-performing organisation where everyone can contribute, grow and succeed together.

Find out more about our people and One FSP Playbook: About FSP | One FSP Playbook




Why work for FSP?

At FSP, we are committed to providing:

A collaborative and supportive environment in which you can grow and develop your career
The tools and opportunity to do work you can be proud of
A chance to work alongside some of the best people in the industry, who always seek to share their knowledge and experience
Hybrid working – we empower you to make smart choices about when and where to work to achieve great results
Industry leading coaching and mentoring
Competitive salary and an excellent benefits package


Equal and Fair Opportunity

FSP is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome applications from all suitable candidates. We consider all applicants for employment regardless of age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief.

Research suggests that applicants from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply for roles if they do not precisely meet requirements, or if they felt there were clear barriers as to who should apply. If you are excited about a potential role with us but are concerned that you may not be a perfect fit, please do apply, as you may be the ideal candidate for this role or for a different vacancy within FSP.

We endeavour to always provide fair opportunity for applicants to showcase themselves in the best way possible during any interviews or meetings. If you require any adjustments for a call or in-person meeting, please let us know.

Graduate Programme 2027 - Technology Risk Auditing
Menzies is an equal opportunities employer which means that we recruit, employ, train, pay, and promote regardless of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, disability or age. We are building a first-class team and, to do so, we know that we need a diverse mix of talented people doing their best work.


About us 

At Menzies LLP, we are dedicated to being a leading firm of advisers and accountants for individuals and businesses. Our approach is driven by BRIGHTER THINKING — combining finance expertise with strategic insight, all while staying true to our core values: Inspire, Innovate, Collaborate, and Empathise.

Proudly recognised as one of the Best Graduate & Apprenticeship Employers for the past five years by JobCrowd.com, we are committed to nurturing future talent.


CISA Qualification

The Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) qualification is awarded by ISACA, a globally recognised professional association specialising in IT governance, risk, cybersecurity and assurance.


As part of the qualification, you’ll develop knowledge across IT auditing, governance, risk management, information security and technology controls. It will help you build the skills to assess systems and processes, identify potential risks and provide assurance that technology is being managed effectively and securely.

What does our Technology Risk team do?
Our Technology Risk team carries out detailed, risk based reviews of a company’s IT environment to determine whether these are managed securely, that data integrity is maintained and that resilience is in place.


We look to challenge the IT organisation of a company and help to improve the internal IT processes as well as providing feedback on how key technology-based risks can be mitigated.  This is an increasingly critical role as companies seek to automate more of their business processes, the increase in cyber attacks and the rapid utilisation of technologies such as AI

What do we look for?
✔️ Individuals who are collaborative and eager to take on new challenges
✔️ A minimum of a 2:2 undergraduate degree in any degree discipline
✔️ Minimum of 2 x A levels (A-C) and one other A level or equivalent
✔️ 5 GCSEs grades A*-C or 9-4 (including Maths and English Language or equivalent)
